en: Sutta Nipāta 5.7 Upasīvamāṇavapucchā “Alone, O Sakka, I have crossed the great flood;”
(Thus spoke the Venerable Upasīva:
"I am unable to cross over without support;
O All-Seeing One, tell me the object [of meditation]."
“Relying on what might I cross over this flood?
“Contemplating nothingness, mindful,” said the Blessed One, “(O Upasīva).”
Relying on "it does not exist," cross over the flood;
having abandoned sensual pleasures and abstaining from talk,
look well toward the destruction of craving at night.
“He who is free from passion for all sensual pleasures,
(thus said the Venerable Upasīva),
relying on the state of nothingness and having abandoned the conceit ‘I am’;”
“Being liberated in the supreme liberation through perception,
would he remain there without following after anything?
“He who is free from passion for all sensual pleasures...”
"Upasīva," said the Blessed One,
"relying on nothingness and abandoning conceit,
you are liberated in the supreme liberation of perception."
“He would stand there, not following after [them].
“If he were to stand there, O All-Seeing One, for even a multitude of years, not following after [them]...”
“Right there he would be cooled and liberated;
for one such as that, consciousness would pass away.
“Just as a flame cast by the force of the wind,”
"It passes away and cannot be defined," said the Blessed One.
"In this way, the sage is liberated from the body of names."
“He passes away and cannot be reckoned.
“Has he set out of existence, or does he not exist?
Or is he indeed forever free from disease?”
“O Sage, explain this well to me,
for this Dhamma is known to you.
“There is no measure for one who has passed away;”
"Upasīva," said the Blessed One,
"that by which one might be described does not exist for him;
when all phenomena have been extinguished."
“All paths of speech have been utterly destroyed.
This is the sixth inquiry of the youth Upasīva.
